exposure: Ongoing respiratory infections in the nursing infant
outcome: Homing of T and B lymphocyte subsets to breast milk
T and B cell subset numbers in milk
Expression of homing receptors (CCR5, CCR6, CCR10, CXCR3) in milk lymphocytes
Maternal serum and milk chemokine levels
Maternal serum and milk cytokine levels
Maternal serum and milk IgA antibody levels
Maternal serum and milk IgG antibody levels
cohort: The study included healthy mothers of nurslings, divided into a group whose infants had ongoing respiratory infections and a control group whose infants were healthy.
finding: Respiratory infections in nursing infants lead to increased cytokines, chemokines, total IgA, and IgG levels in breast milk, facilitating the recruitment and activation of various T and B lymphocyte subsets expressing specific homing receptors.
cross-section timing: Mature milk and blood samples were collected at a single point in time, corresponding to whether the nursling had an ongoing respiratory infection or was healthy.
